edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 24 November 2026 and 10:00 AM IST on 25 November 2026

items.coram: Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member) and Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLAT upholds two-year suspension of RP in Revital Reality CIRP and lays out a framework for IBBI disciplinary orders
items.text: The appellate tribunal upheld the IBBI disciplinary committee's two-year suspension of insolvency professional Gaurav Katiyar, effective 21 August 2026. It found two lapses: he let a consortium revise its plan and file documents after the CoC's deadline without approval, and he dropped a five-year recency requirement from the eligibility criteria without recording reasons. It also suggested a detailed structure that future IBBI disciplinary orders should follow.

items.coram: Mahavir Singh (Vice President) and S. Rifaur Rahman (Accountant Member)
items.headline: ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 140.70 crore additions against Hero MotoCorp chief Pawan Munjal
items.text: After a 2022 search, the Assessing Officer had added Rs 35.28 crore as an unexplained investment in Chhatarpur land and Rs 105.41 crore as perquisites, and Rs 26.14 crore of the perquisite addition was still in dispute after the first appeal. The tribunal allowed Munjal's appeals and dismissed the Revenue's, finding no proof that he made the alleged cash-funded land investment. It held that a company's disallowance of expenses under Section 37(1) does not by itself make them taxable perquisites in an employee's hands.

items.caseName: Tata Sons Private Limited v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax
items.coram: Amit Shukla (Judicial Member) and G.M. Doss (Accountant Member)
items.headline: ITAT Mumbai allows Tata Sons' interest deduction on borrowings used for group investments
items.text: For AY 2014-15, the Assessing Officer had refused Tata Sons' deduction for interest on borrowings used to invest in group companies and disallowed Rs 1,522.40 crore under Section 14A, which the CIT(A) cut to Rs 578.56 crore. The tribunal dismissed the Revenue's appeal, holding that a Section 14A disallowance does not by itself negate the business purpose of a borrowing. It also held that the Rule 8D figure cannot be added mechanically to book profit under Section 115JB.

items.caseName: Canara Bank v. Keshav Ashok Punj & Raghav Ashok Punj
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) and Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Ahmedabad admits Canara Bank's Rs 1,742 crore insolvency pleas against PSL's personal guarantors
items.text: Canara Bank had filed Section 95 petitions against the two personal guarantors of PSL Limited, which is in liquidation, to recover about Rs 1,742.75 crore. The bench held that the guarantors' default date must be fixed under each guarantee and is not automatically the corporate debtor's default date. Rejecting the waiver, forgery and limitation objections, partly on res judicata from an earlier DRT finding, it admitted both petitions and imposed a Section 101 moratorium.

items.caseName: Mohit Chawla, RP of Krishna Knitwear Technology Limited v. The Assessing Officer, DCIT Central Circle 5(3), Mumbai, Income Tax Department
items.caseNo: IA No. 1703 (AHM) of 2026 in CP (IB) No. 279 (AHM) of 2018
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) and Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Ahmedabad: Income Tax Department cannot adjust refunds against dues during the IBC moratorium
items.text: During the CIRP of Krishna Knitwear Technology, the Income Tax Department had adjusted refunds of Rs 26,41,770 for AYs 2018-19 to 2025-26 against claimed tax demands. Hearing the matter ex parte after the department did not appear, the bench held that Section 245 of the Income-tax Act permits such adjustments in general but they cannot be made during CIRP, given Sections 14 and 238 of the IBC. It set aside the adjustments and ordered the money restored to the company's account.

items.caseName: The Nasik Merchants Co-operative Bank Ltd. v. Kailash T Shah
items.coram: Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member) and Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLAT: An RP's approved monthly fee stays in force until the CoC or the NCLT alters it
items.text: A secured creditor challenged an order requiring it to pay Rs 16.48 lakh in CIRP costs and fees to the RP of Yug Weave Tech, arguing that it had ratified fees only up to October 2021. The appellate tribunal noted that the CoC had fixed the fee at Rs 1 lakh a month in November 2020 and never revised it, and that only the CoC, through a specific agenda item, or the Adjudicating Authority could change it. It dismissed the appeal, so the bank must pay the fees up to liquidation on 6 July 2022.

items.caseName: Dr. Hirenkumar Vipinchandra Shah v. Dr. Nainesh Bhanubhai Patel & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Indevar Pandey (Technical Member) and Arun Baroka (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLAT imposes Rs 2 lakh costs over an appeal against a mere notice order in an oppression case
items.text: A major shareholder of Adajan Health Care appealed after the NCLT ordered notice on his Sections 241-242 petition without first ruling on a maintainability objection. The appellate tribunal held that maintainability is a mixed question of fact and law that ordinarily needs notice to all parties first. Calling the appeal an abuse of process, it dismissed it with Rs 2 lakh in costs payable to the PM's Relief Fund.

items.caseName: SA Engineering (Through its Sole Proprietor – Shahin Contractor) v. M/s. Shapoorji Pallonji & Co. Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: K.R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Mumbai: Payments on one project cannot extend limitation for dues on other projects
items.text: SA Engineering sought insolvency against Shapoorji Pallonji over about Rs 1.24 crore for structural steel work across projects in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Because the creditor kept project-wise ledgers, the bench held that payments on one project extended limitation only for that project, so Rs 36.07 lakh was time-barred, and it also found Rs 58.34 lakh of retention money not shown to be due. With the rest of the claim below the Rs 1 crore threshold, the petition was dismissed without prejudice to other remedies.

items.caseName: Sunil Kumar Singh & Ors. v. IVR Prime IT SEZ Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
items.coram: Jyotsna Sharma (Judicial Member) and Reena Sinha Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Delhi: Homebuyers must raise CIRP objections through their Authorised Representative
items.text: Twenty-eight homebuyers asked the bench to defer consideration of Sloan Solutions' resolution plan in the CIRP of IVR Prime IT SEZ, saying its termination of a development agreement would hurt their rights. The bench held that members of a creditor class must raise objections through the Authorised Representative and cannot approach the Adjudicating Authority directly. Finding they had no locus because they were not a class of creditors in this CIRP, it dismissed the application as infructuous.

items.caseName: Smartworks Coworking Spaces Limited v. Registrar of Companies
items.coram: Mahnedra Khandelwal (Judicial Member) and Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Delhi issues notice to regulators and creditors on Smartworks' Rs 385.61 crore capital reduction plea
items.text: Smartworks Coworking Spaces seeks confirmation under Sections 66 and 52 of the Companies Act to use about Rs 385.61 crore from its securities premium account to write off accumulated losses, without changing its share capital. The bench gave the Central Government (through the Regional Director), the RoC and SEBI 90 days to object, and directed the company to notify creditors, who have three months to respond. The matter is next listed on 23 February 2027.

items.caseName: In the matter of Scheme of Arrangement Between Indiannica Learning Private Limited With Navneet Education Limited
items.coram: K.R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Mumbai sanctions demerger of Indiannica Learning's publishing business into Navneet Education
items.text: The bench sanctioned a composite scheme under Sections 230-232 and 66 transferring the publishing business of wholly owned subsidiary Indiannica Learning to Navneet Education as a going concern, with an appointed date of 1 April 2025. The scheme also cuts Indiannica's share capital and securities premium by Rs 126.77 crore to clear the debit balance in its reserves, and no shares are issued. The Regional Director withdrew its objections after the companies gave clarifications and undertakings.

items.caseName: Nikhath Fathima v. Maschmeijer Aromatics India Private Limited & Ors.
items.coram: Jyoti Kumar Tripathi (Judicial Member) and Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Chennai: A company cannot keep a share transfer request pending indefinitely over internal disputes
items.text: The petitioner sought registration of 87 shares gifted to her by her late mother-in-law, whose transfer documents the company had received in January 2021 but never acted on. Rejecting objections based on a 1991 shareholders' agreement that was never incorporated into the articles and on board deadlock, the bench allowed her Section 58 petition. It directed registration and rectification of the register of members, subject to her paying any stamp duty deficit.

items.caseName: Medicare Environmental Management Private Limited v. Sunil Kumar, Additional Commissioner of State Tax, Muzaffarpur East Tirhut, Bihar & Ors.
items.coram: Manoj Kumar Sinha (Judicial Member) and Sanjay Kumar Mawandia (Technical Member)
items.headline: GSTAT Patna: A GST-VAT turnover mismatch cannot create GST liability for pre-GST months
items.text: A biomedical waste management company was assessed on a difference of about Rs 1.03 crore between its GSTR-9C turnover and its Bihar VAT return for April to June 2017, before GST came into force. The tribunal held that a turnover mismatch alone cannot establish GST liability, since pre-GST liability falls under the earlier laws. It set aside the tax, interest and penalty and remanded the matter for fresh adjudication on the new material.

items.caseName: M/s F.I.T. Brick Field v. Ramesh Chandra Dubey, Additional Commissioner Grade-II (Appeal), State Tax, Sitapur & Ors.
items.coram: Santosh Kumar Srivastava (Judicial Member) and Arvind Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: GSTAT Lucknow: Coal purchases alone cannot prove a brick kiln suppressed turnover
items.text: The department had estimated higher 2018-19 sales for a composition-scheme brick kiln in Sitapur from its coal purchases and confirmed a demand ex parte. The tribunal held that coal purchases alone cannot establish suppressed turnover and that a composition taxpayer cannot face an excess ITC demand. It set aside the orders and remanded the matter for fresh adjudication after verifying the records and giving a hearing.

items.caseName: Satish Kumar Pandey and Sangeeta Pandey v. Century Real Estate Holdings Private Limited and Karthik Shankarlingegowda alias Karthik S
items.headline: Karnataka RERA: Developer cannot undervalue a resold flat to deny the original buyers a refund with interest
items.text: The complainants had agreed in 2014 to buy a flat worth about Rs 2.88 crore in Century's Bengaluru project, and the possession deadline of 20 July 2020 was missed. They later found the developer had already resold the flat in May 2024 while resale talks were under way. The Authority held that the higher resale value must be taken into account and directed Century and the subsequent buyer to jointly pay about Rs 5.75 crore, with interest from 20 July 2020.

items.caseName: Sachin Kumar v. ITO, Ward 4(1), Gurgaon
items.coram: S. Rifaur Rahman (Accountant Member) and Raj Kumar Chauhan (Judicial Member)
items.headline: ITAT Delhi: A missing field verification report does not make a faceless assessment erroneous under Section 263
items.text: The assessee sold ancestral farm land for Rs 25.80 crore and claimed Section 54B and 54F deductions, and the faceless assessment was completed before a physical verification report arrived. The PCIT set the assessment aside under Section 263. The tribunal quashed the revision, holding that a pending report from an internal unit does not by itself make the assessment erroneous and that no error had been shown under the faceless scheme.

items.headline: ITAT Delhi: Ten-year reopening limit after a search cannot be stretched; Rs 16.91 crore reassessment quashed
items.text: After a 2022 search, the AY 2012-13 income of the Prudence Group of Schools chairperson was reassessed with a Rs 16.91 crore addition under Section 68. The tribunal dismissed the Revenue's appeal and upheld the quashing of the reassessment. It held the Section 148 notice was time-barred because the ten-year period under the first proviso to Section 149(1)(b) cannot go beyond the limit under the pre-2021 provisions.

items.headline: ITAT Rajkot: A digital marketer is not a 'professional' just because payers deducted TDS under Section 194J
items.text: The assessee, who runs an e-commerce facilitation and digital marketing business, offered income at 8.18% of turnover under Section 44AD for AY 2024-25. An addition of Rs 14.63 lakh was made by treating his receipts as 50% professional income under Section 44ADA. The tribunal deleted it, holding that TDS under Section 194J does not turn a digital marketer into someone practising a specified profession.

items.headline: CESTAT Mumbai: Retracted statements cannot justify raising the customs value of 129 used cranes
items.text: The dispute covered 129 second-hand cranes imported between 2006 and 2010, directly and through high-sea sales, whose value had been enhanced on the basis of chartered engineers' estimates and the importer's statements. The tribunal held that statements the importer had withdrawn could not, without corroborating material, support raising the declared value. It set aside the duty demands and penalties.
